text.content: Magic in the wilds of Veradyna is a test of will and focus.

How a spell lands: its target saves, or the spell simply works. No spell rolls to hit, rays and ranged spells included, except a Touch spell against an unwilling creature (see Spell Targeting).

Saving Throws

  • When: any spell that damages or debuffs a target (for example Fireball, Hold Person, Fear, Ray of Enfeeblement, Blindness/Deafness).
  • Spell DC: 10 + half your caster level (rounded down, minimum 1) + your casting-stat modifier.
    • Your caster level is your level in that class.
    • Your DC is the same for every spell you cast.
  • The save: the target rolls d20 + its save + half its level (rounded down, minimum 1). It succeeds if the total meets or beats the DC.
    • The spell names the save: Fortitude (Constitution modifier), Reflex (Dexterity modifier) or Will (Wisdom modifier).
    • Advantage and Disadvantage apply as normal.
    • A natural 20 always succeeds and a natural 1 always fails, whatever the total, as with attack rolls.
  • Monsters and NPCs: use the same DC formula when they cast. Against a PC's spell, a monster rolls the save printed in its stat block against the caster's DC.
  • Concentration: a spell marked (concentration) lasts only while you keep your focus.
    • You can hold one at a time.
    • It ends if you take damage and fail the Fortitude save, if you are Stunned, Paralysed or Unconscious, or if you cast another concentration spell.
    • See Concentration in Section II of The Arneyan Codex.

Example: A 6th-level Cleric (Wisdom 16, +2) casts Hold Person at a 3rd-level bandit (Wisdom 13, +1). The DC is 10 + 3 + 2 = 15. The bandit rolls d20 + 1 + 1 and is Paralysed unless it reaches 15: a 40% chance to resist.

Automatic Spells

  • When: spells that buff, aid or give a utility effect with no hostile target, and spells that strike with no save (for example Invisibility, Shield, Bless, Cure Light Wounds, Magic Missile).
  • Resolving: no roll. The spell works.

Preparing and Casting

  • Preparation: each morning, choose your prepared spells from the spells you have access to. You can prepare a number of different spells equal to your caster level + your casting-stat modifier (minimum 1).
  • Slots: you have a set number of slots of each level. Spend a slot to cast any prepared spell of that level.
  • Bonus slots: a high casting stat gives extra slots, cumulatively.
    • 13 to 15: one extra 1st-level slot.
    • 16 to 17: also one extra 2nd-level slot.
    • 18 or more: also one extra 3rd-level slot.
    • A bonus slot arrives only once your class table gives you slots of that level. You can only prepare or know spells of a level your table gives you slots for.
    • A Bard also knows one extra spell of each of those levels. A Sorcerer gains an extra spell known as well as the slot (see Sorcerer).
  • Casting time: casting a spell takes your action unless the spell says otherwise. The spell takes effect on your turn, but damage taken while you cast can make you lose it (see Casting Under Threat in The Arneyan Codex).
  • Scaling: every spell grows stronger as you level. You can cast a lower-level spell with a higher-level slot, but its potency (damage, duration and the like) is always set by your caster level.

Spell Targeting

  • Path and sight: you need a clear path to the target or area, and you must be able to see it.
  • Touch spells: you must be adjacent.
    • Against an unwilling creature, make a touch attack: d20 + BtH + your casting modifier against its AC. It replaces the save. A hit gives the full effect, a miss none. A monster uses its attack bonus.
    • An ally is touched automatically.
    • Spells that set a ward or trap on a surface keep their saves.
  • Alignment in spells: a spell that names Good, Evil, Law, Chaos or an alignment means a creature's Allegiance (see Taking a Side in Character Creation). An Unaligned creature counts as none of them, so such a spell passes it by unless it says otherwise.

Illusions and Disbelief

  • Belief: a creature that perceives an illusion believes it until it has reason to doubt.
  • The save: it makes a Will save against the caster's DC when it touches the illusion, is harmed by it, or spends its action studying it. A spell's entry may add other triggers.
  • Success: it sees through that illusion for as long as the illusion lasts. It is no longer harmed or hindered by it, and others it warns save with Advantage.
  • Failure: it believes, and saves again only when something new gives it reason to doubt (the GM's call).
  • True Seeing and truesight see through illusions with no save.

Changing Shape

  • The form: a spell or feature that changes a creature's form (Polymorph, Shapechange, Wild Shape and similar) gives it the new form's whole stat block from Monsters & Treasure: HP, AC, attacks, saves and movement.
  • What it keeps: its own mind, personality and alignment.
  • At 0 HP: it returns to its own form with the HP it had when it changed. Damage beyond 0 does not carry over.
  • Level: the spell or feature caps the form's Level.

Summoned and Conjured Attackers

  • One at a time: unless a spell or feature says otherwise, you can have only one spell-made attacker at a time. Casting another ends the first.
    • A spell-made attacker is a summoned creature (or the group from one summoning), or anything a spell creates that attacks or deals damage on its own each round: Spiritual Weapon, Summon Swarm, Animate Objects, Mordenkainen's Sword, Faithful Hound, the Bigby's hands, Shadow Monsters, Changestaff and the like.
    • Walls, clouds and areas are not attackers. Familiars and mounts don't count.
  • Acting: summoned creatures act straight after you in the initiative order and obey your spoken commands.
  • Solos: a creature marked Solo is never summoned, called, conjured or taken as a form. A creature of its Level without the mark is the most a spell gives.
  • Class companions: a companion, construct or mount from a class feature is not a spell-made attacker; you command it.
  • Raised undead follow their own control limits instead (the Necromancer's Undead Mastery).

Levels

  • Where a spell or ability names a Level ("creatures of Level 4 or lower"), it means a creature's Level in Monsters & Treasure, or a character's level.
  • Hit Dice still set a creature's HP and the totals for raising undead.

Slots, Recovery and Learning Spells

  • Slot recovery: a long rest restores all your spent slots. Casters who prepare spells choose their prepared list again after the rest.
  • Reading the tables: in a Spells Per Day table, the 0 column is the number of cantrips you have. Every other column is the number of slots of that spell level.
  • Starting spells:
    • Spellbook casters (Wizard, Illusionist, Necromancer, Spellblade) begin with a spellbook holding all their cantrips and six 1st-level spells of their choice from their class list.
    • Clerics, Druids, Paladins and Witches prepare each morning from their whole class list.
    • Bards, Sorcerers and Warlocks know a fixed set of spells (see their classes).
  • Gaining spells:
    • A spellbook caster who gains a level adds two spells of a level they can cast to their spellbook, free.
    • Any other spell, from another spellbook or a scroll, is copied at the cost in IX.
    • Casters who need no book learn new spells as their class describes.

Schools and Traditions

  • Tags: every spell in the Master Spell List carries a tag under its name.
  • Arcane schools:
    • Abjuration: wards and protection.
    • Conjuration: summoning, creation and travel.
    • Divination: knowledge and sight.
    • Enchantment: charm and compulsion.
    • Evocation: raw energy and force.
    • Illusion: false senses.
    • Necromancy: death, life and the undead.
    • Transmutation: changing the nature of things.
  • Traditions:
    • Arcane casters: Wizard, Illusionist, Necromancer, Sorcerer, Warlock, Witch, Bard and Spellblade.
    • Divine casters: Cleric and Paladin.
    • Nature casters: Druid.
    • A spell on no arcane list is tagged Divine, Nature or both. A spell on an arcane list and on a divine or nature list keeps its arcane school; the Classes column shows everyone who can cast it.
  • School Focus: a Wizard picks a school at 1st level and gets an extra slot that casts only one prepared spell of that school (two from 10th).
  • Favoured schools: some arcane casters add every Wizard-list spell of their favoured schools, up to the highest spell level they can cast. Spells your class or kit excludes are never gained this way.
    • Sorcerer: Evocation and Transmutation; not Time Stop, Forcecage, Permanency or Polymorph Any Object.
    • Witch: Enchantment, Necromancy and Divination; not Power Word Stun, Power Word Blind or Power Word Kill.
    • Bard: Enchantment, Illusion and Divination.
    • Spellblade: Evocation and Abjuration; not Stoneskin or Melf's Minute Meteors.

• At will: a cantrip uses no slot.
  • Always prepared: cantrips you know are always prepared and never count against your prepared spells.
  • Damaging or debuffing cantrips: the target saves against your spell DC.
  • Utility cantrips: no roll.
  • Scaling: a cantrip gains its extra dice at caster level 5, 11 and 17.

Solos (Running a Solo, Monsters & Treasure) are hard to control for long: spells always work on them, but they shake control off quickly.

  • Control effects: an effect that stops a solo acting, attacking, moving or casting as it normally would ends once the solo has spent two of its turns under it.
    • This covers Incapacitated, Paralysed, Stunned, Unconscious, Charmed, Dominated, Confused, Slowed, Restrained, Blinded, Frightened, Feeblemind, Polymorph, Exhaustion from a spell and the like.
  • Banishing and imprisoning: an effect that would banish it, imprison it or turn it to stone (Banishment, Maze, Forcecage, Temporal Stasis and the like) works the same way: the solo comes back or breaks free once it has spent two of its turns that way.
  • Kill effects: an effect that would kill it outright (Power Word Kill, Disintegrate and the like) instead deals damage equal to its current HP.
  • After shaking one off:
    • No effect of these kinds can affect it again until the end of the following round.
    • The second time in one fight it shakes one off, the effect ends after one of its turns instead.
  • Exhaustion: a solo ignores Exhaustion's Max HP loss.
  • Phases: a solo fights in three phases.
    • At 0 HP its next phase starts at full HP. Damage beyond 0 is lost, and every condition and hostile spell or effect on it ends.
    • It dies at 0 HP in its third phase.

There is no spell resistance. Some magical creatures have Magic Resistance: Advantage on saves against spells.

• Training: you cannot cast spells in armour you are not trained in.
  • Classes with "None": a class that lists "None" is trained in no armour, so wearing any armour or carrying a shield blocks its casting.
  • War Caster: the feat can grant training in one type of Light or Medium armour, or a shield.
  • Other training: only a feat, or a kit that says so, lets a class that lists "None" cast in armour. Training from another class, an ancestry or downtime removes the penalties for wearing armour, never the block on casting.

• Verbal (V): you must be able to speak. Silence, a gag or the like stops V spells.
  • Somatic (S): you need at least one free hand, and a grappled caster can't cast S spells (see Grapple in The Arneyan Codex). Armour and shields don't matter if you are trained in them (see VI).
  • Material (M): a component or focus.
    • Common components are free if you carry a spellcasting focus.
    • A rare component must be acquired before the spell can be cast.
  • Saves:
    • Fortitude: body, poison, death, petrification, sickness.
    • Reflex: dodging blasts and areas.
    • Will: mind, charm, fear, illusion.
    • In the spell list, "—" means no save, and Touch means a touch attack replaces it (see Spell Targeting).
    • For a reversible (*) spell, the Save column shows the save of whichever form is harmful.
    • A damage spell with a save deals half damage on a success, unless its entry says the save negates.
  • Ritual: you can cast a spell tagged Ritual from your prepared list without spending a slot by taking an extra 10 minutes. Not in combat. A spell with its own Ritual text (Wish, Miracle) follows that text instead.
  • Reversible (*): you may cast the opposite effect (Cure Light Wounds or Cause Light Wounds) with the same slot.
    • Cure spells heal an ally with no roll.
    • Against an undead, a cure spell needs a touch attack, and its healing deals radiant damage.
    • A Cause Wounds spell heals an undead instead.

• Dying, not dead: a dying character can still be stabilised (see Death & Dying in The Arneyan Codex). The methods below apply only once the character is dead.
  • No return: nothing returns a creature whose soul is unwilling (the player decides), trapped (Soul Bind, Trap the Soul, Magic Jar) or raised as undead, or whose spell's time limit or body requirement is not met.

  • Wish and Miracle: cast as a ritual (1 hour; 2,500 gp of components for Wish or 1,000 gp of offerings for Miracle; the caster takes 2 levels of Exhaustion). It returns one dead creature as True Resurrection, with no body or time limit. Raising the dead this way also consumes diamond dust worth 25,000 gp.
  • Afterwards: Exhaustion from a return fades as normal (see Fatigue & Exhaustion). A returned character has no spells prepared, and keeps its level, class, memories and recovered gear.

Spellbooks

  • Who keeps one: Wizards, Illusionists, Necromancers and Spellblades.
  • Pages: a spellbook (1 slot) holds 100 pages. A spell takes pages equal to its level; a cantrip takes 1.
  • Preparing: you can only prepare spells from a spellbook you have in hand, or from a copy of it.
  • Copying a spell: from another caster's spellbook or from a scroll, if the spell is on your class list. It takes 1 day and 5 gp per spell level (the Learn Spells cost), with no roll. A copied scroll is used up.
  • Foreign and locked writing: a book in a strange cipher, or one sealed with magic, needs Read Magic before you can copy from it.
  • A lost or destroyed book: you keep and cast your prepared spells, but cannot change them until you have a book again.
  • Hazards: fire, acid or an hour in water ruins a spellbook.

Scrolls

  • Contents: a scroll holds one spell, and crumbles when it is cast.
  • Who can use one: anyone.
    • A caster of the scroll's tradition (arcane, or divine and nature) knows what it holds at a glance.
    • Anyone else must have it identified, or read it blind; its spell shows only as it takes effect.
    • Casting from a scroll needs no slot or components, but you must speak and gesture.
  • Identified scrolls: once Identify or research reveals a scroll's spell, you cast it with no check, whatever your class or level.
  • Reading blind: make a casting-stat check (Intelligence if you have none) against DC 10 + the spell's level. On a failure the scroll is wasted.
  • Potency: a scroll keeps its writer's caster level and save DC. One of unknown origin, or read by someone outside its tradition, casts at caster level 2 × spell level − 1 (minimum 1) with DC 12 + spell level.
  • Writing one: you must know the spell.
    • It takes 1 week and 10 gp per spell level (a cantrip: 1 day and 1 gp), plus costly components.
    • You can write no more scrolls a month than your casting-stat modifier (minimum 1).
  • Fire and price: scrolls burn easily; a case holds 5. Scrolls of 8th level and up are never sold; the Catalogue prices the rest.

All spells available in Arneyan, with the save the target rolls (Fortitude, Reflex or Will; — means automatic, no save), the components needed, and a Ritual tag where a spell can be cast as a ritual. Class-only and Path spells appear in their class chapters; they count as spells of that class for scrolls, Counterspell and Dispel Magic. * = reversible spell. ‡ = needs a costed material component (see Rare Spell Components in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue; for a cost by HD, a character counts its level). Classes listed are those with access in this campaign — Wizard (Wiz), Illusionist (Ill), Cleric (Cle), Druid (Dru), Warlock (War), Sorcerer (Sor), Bard (Bar), Paladin (Pal), Spellblade (Spb), Necromancer (Nec), Witch (Wit).
Cantrips do not consume spell slots and can be cast at will.
Every spell is in the Spells compendium, sorted by level. Drag a spell onto a character sheet to add it.
